svg.title: $575,000 Resale Proceeds Become $80,500 Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $575,000 Resale Proceeds Become $80,500 Owner Net; subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical Base-Case 14.0% net margin; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: USD per year. Opening and closing bars are totals; the four intermediate bars are negative cost movements. The scorecard fixes revenue and owner net, while the cost-category split is an illustrative operating budget. Direct handling and repair labor belong in their respective direct-cost categories; remaining operating labor belongs in overhead.; caption: $575,000 - $345,000 - $46,000 - $46,000 - $57,500 = $80,500; $80,500 / $575,000 = 14.0%. Sales tax collected for remittance is excluded from resale revenue.; stages: label: Gross resale proceeds; value: $575,000 opening total; numeric value: 575000.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case annual operator revenue from owned surplus inventory resales. This is neither client asset value nor a marketplace's aggregate transaction volume.; label: Inventory acquisition; value: -$345,000; 60% of revenue; numeric value: -345000.0; detail: Allocate purchase prices, buyer premiums, and nonrecoverable acquisition taxes to units sold. Recoverable taxes are excluded; unsold inventory remains a separate working-capital exposure.; label: Transport and handling; value: -$46,000; 8% of revenue; numeric value: -46000.0; detail: Include loading, rigging, carrier charges, fuel surcharges, direct handling labor, and delivery costs associated with completed resales. Missed pickup windows can exhaust this entire allowance.; label: Inspection and refurbishment; value: -$46,000; 8% of revenue; numeric value: -46000.0; detail: Budget inspection effort, parts, testing, cleaning, and repair-contractor labor. Include inspections that produce no winning bid and avoid counting the same labor again in overhead.; label: Operating overhead; value: -$57,500; 10% of revenue; numeric value: -57500.0; detail: Allocate remaining operating labor, storage, insurance, software, selling and payment fees, administration, and operating-loss allowances. The monthly equivalent is $4,791.67, within the canonical $3,000–$15,000 monthly opex range.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $80,500 closing total; 14.0%; numeric value: 80500.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case residual after the four expense categories for a two-full-time, three-contractor pod. Owner distributions do not create an additional expense below this closing total.

rect.title: label: Gross resale proceeds; value: $575,000 opening total; numeric value: 575000.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case annual operator revenue from owned surplus inventory resales. This is neither client asset value nor a marketplace's aggregate transaction volume.

label: Inventory acquisition; value: -$345,000; 60% of revenue; numeric value: -345000.0; detail: Allocate purchase prices, buyer premiums, and nonrecoverable acquisition taxes to units sold. Recoverable taxes are excluded; unsold inventory remains a separate working-capital exposure.

label: Transport and handling; value: -$46,000; 8% of revenue; numeric value: -46000.0; detail: Include loading, rigging, carrier charges, fuel surcharges, direct handling labor, and delivery costs associated with completed resales. Missed pickup windows can exhaust this entire allowance.

label: Inspection and refurbishment; value: -$46,000; 8% of revenue; numeric value: -46000.0; detail: Budget inspection effort, parts, testing, cleaning, and repair-contractor labor. Include inspections that produce no winning bid and avoid counting the same labor again in overhead.

label: Operating overhead; value: -$57,500; 10% of revenue; numeric value: -57500.0; detail: Allocate remaining operating labor, storage, insurance, software, selling and payment fees, administration, and operating-loss allowances. The monthly equivalent is $4,791.67, within the canonical $3,000–$15,000 monthly opex range.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $80,500 closing total; 14.0%; numeric value: 80500.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case residual after the four expense categories for a two-full-time, three-contractor pod. Owner distributions do not create an additional expense below this closing total.

text.title: Assumptions: USD per year. Opening and closing bars are totals; the four intermediate bars are negative cost movements. The scorecard fixes revenue and owner net, while the cost-category split is an illustrative operating budget. Direct handling and repair labor belong in their respective direct-cost categories; remaining operating labor belongs in overhead.
